author.name: Ray Bradbury
author.heading: About Ray Bradbury
author.bio: Ray Bradbury wrote The Martian Chronicles and Fahrenheit 451, but also wrote about the practical pleasure of writing. In Zen in the Art of Writing, he collected essays urging writers to trust enthusiasm and keep working.

cite.sourceCitation: Bradbury, Ray. Zen in the Art of Writing.1990. Sentence credited through LibQuotes and quoted by WIRED; original page unconfirmed.

copyAttribution: — Attributed to Ray Bradbury, Zen in the Art of Writing; original page unconfirmed.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Drunk on writing is a figure of speech for absorption and enthusiasm, not a demonstrated instruction to drink alcohol. The official writing page ↗ describes writing as a tonic against everyday sorrows and sets that idea beside the discipline of regular practice.
